title: E-Series Preferred Values
summary: the standard preferred resistor/capacitor value sets (E6/E12/E24) and why they are spaced logarithmically.
body:
components come in preferred values spaced so that tolerance bands tile the
range with minimal overlap. E12 (10% tolerance) has 12 values per decade, E24
(5%) has 24, E6 (20%) has 6. multiply any base value by a power of ten to reach
other decades (e.g. 4.7 -> 47, 470, 4.7k...).
examples: need ~3.1k at 5%: nearest E24 is 3.0k or 3.3k.
need ~5k: not an E12 value; use 4.7k (E12) or combine 4.7k + 330 in series.
gotchas: 5000 ohm and 2000 ohm are NOT standard values; common mistakes are 4.7k/5.1k and 2.0k/2.2k
E96 (1%) and E192 (0.5%) exist for precision work with 96 and 192 values per decade
